methods.description: Count marked vertices and individual edges; read the other vertices directly joined by an edge. Count parallel edges separately and a loop as one edge; an unmarked crossing does not add a vertex.
Count the edge-ends meeting a vertex, including each parallel edge separately and both ends of a loop. Interpret a larger degree as more connections, without inferring greater traffic.

Add the vertex degrees and check twice the edge count, or divide the total by two to find the edges. Each edge contributes two ends, including loops. This is elementary counting from the source degree definition/loop figure, not a separate advanced named theorem.

Compare the edge pairs between the same named vertices. Moving vertices or bending edges preserves a network if those connections (and any directions/weights) remain unchanged. Equal counts or an equal list of degrees alone do not establish identical named connections.
Follow the arrow from its starting vertex to identify an allowed direct trip. An incoming arrow does not permit the reverse trip, and a journey using two edges is not direct.
Identify the single requested edge and read its weight using the stated contextual unit. Opposite directed edges may have different weights; do not substitute another edge or add a route.
